days.title: Fort Kochi on foot — spice lanes, nets and a Kathakali face

stops.title: Kerala sadya lunch in Fort Kochi
stops.notes: Banana-leaf lunch — rice, sambar, avial, and a fish fry on the side

stops.title: Mattancherry Palace (Dutch Palace)
stops.notes: ₹5 for Indian visitors, one of the cheapest tickets in India for a palace full of Kochi's murals. Jew Town and the Paradesi synagogue lane are the same stop

stops.title: Chinese fishing nets, Fort Kochi beach
stops.notes: The cantilevered nets are worked at high tide; the walk from the Dutch cemetery end is the good half

stops.title: Kathakali performance, Fort Kochi
stops.notes: Most centres let you in 45 minutes early to watch the make-up going on — that half-hour is the real show. Tickets (about ₹300–500) are in the ticket allowance

stops.title: First night in Kochi
stops.notes: A heritage homestay in Fort Kochi beats a city hotel — everything today is within walking distance

days.title: Up the ghats to Munnar — waterfalls, then tea country

stops.title: Cheeyappara waterfalls
stops.notes: Right on the Kochi–Madurai highway, free to stop at; best right after rain, which is most of the year

stops.title: KDHP Tea Museum
stops.notes: The working tea factory tour that explains what you have been driving through. Ticket prices here are revised often — verify at the counter

stops.title: Two nights in Munnar
stops.notes: Take the second night here: the hill station rewards a slow morning more than it rewards another drive

days.title: Eravikulam's mountain goats and the Mattupetty road

stops.title: Eravikulam National Park
stops.notes: Home of the Nilgiri tahr — the park's own booking site lists ₹200 for Indian adults plus a ₹50 reservation fee, and closes the gate at 14:00. Online slots sell out on weekends

stops.title: Mattupetty Dam and its echo point
stops.notes: The dam road is the prettiest drive in Munnar; the small parking and boat charges are collected in cash at the gate (see the ticket allowance)

days.title: Down the spice ghats to Thekkady and Periyar's lake

stops.title: Kumily-side lunch and spice shops
stops.notes: Cardamom, pepper and vanilla straight from the plantation shops on the Kumily road

stops.title: Periyar Tiger Reserve lake boat
stops.notes: Park entry is ₹25/person; the lake boat is a separate booking (₹255 — see the expense line) that sells out a day ahead. Early boats see more wildlife

days.title: Down to the backwaters — board the houseboat at Alappuzha

stops.title: Alappuzha beach and its old pier
stops.notes: Five minutes from the boat jetty — the 150-year-old pier is the photograph before you board

stops.title: Backwater houseboat, Vembanad Lake
stops.notes: Board by early afternoon, cruise the Punnamada and Vembanad channels, moor for the night. The crew cooks — the cost is a premium over a standard room, itemised in the budget

days.title: The slow road home — Kumarakom's birds, then Kochi

stops.title: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
stops.notes: Go early — the sanctuary is at its best between 6 and 9 AM. Small gate and parking charges are cash, in the ticket allowance

stops.title: Late lunch in Kochi
stops.notes: If the flight is late, Marari's fishing-village beach is 30 minutes west of here — the quietest sand in the Alappuzha district

stops.title: Cochin airport drop
stops.notes: 45 minutes from the city; leave three hours before an international departure

publication.title: Kerala Hills & Backwaters — Kochi to Munnar to a Houseboat
publication.tagline: Tea country, a tiger reserve and a night on a houseboat — hills and water in one loop, with the ghats driven downhill and never in a rush.
publication.bestSeason: Sep–Mar — post-monsoon green through the dry winter. Jun–Aug dumps about 2,000 mm on Munnar and the ghats get slick
travelTips: Hire a car with a driver for the whole loop: the Kochi–Munnar ghat road is 100 km of switchbacks and nobody in the family should have to drive it.
Eravikulam sells timed slots online and closes the gate at 2 PM — book the 8 AM entry the night before.
Take the second night in Munnar rather than the second hill station. Two nights in one place is what makes a hill trip restful.
Book the Periyar lake boat when you reach Thekkady, not on the day — the early boats are the ones that see animals.
Board the houseboat by early afternoon. The best hours on the backwaters are the ones before sunset.
warningsAndAssumptions: Entry fees verified Sep 2026: Mattancherry Palace ₹5 (Indian visitors), Periyar park entry ₹25, Eravikulam ₹200 + ₹50 reservation per the park's own booking site.

Eravikulam is quoted between ₹90 and ₹200 across listings — older pages predate the current online-booking tariffs. The park's own site (₹200 Indian adult) is what is published here; expect an advance booking fee on top.
The KDHP Tea Museum ticket is ₹75 per the operator's listing; Munnar's museum pricing is revised regularly, so verify at the counter.

The Alappuzha houseboat is priced as a ₹3,000/person premium over a standard comfort room, because the engine's lodging model has no houseboat tier. Off-season this is cheaper; Christmas week it is far more.
Small gate charges that are collected in cash (Mattupetty, Kumarakom, temple donations, the Kathakali show) are covered by a ₹150 ticket allowance rather than invented line items.
All costs are engine estimates over real coordinates and cited fees, not quotes. Treat ±15% as the honest band.
